content:
**installer: legacy-install fallback and a legible failure (#625)**

Traced the break the scoped rename causes: a consumer's vendored OLD brain-upgrade.mjs resolves node_modules/brain, installSpec returns the git URL, npm reads the NEW package.json and lands the tree under the scope, and the old code dies. That half is unfixable — the code is already in their tree. Fixed the mirror half: new code finding an old install, via resolveInstalledPackageRoot's legacy fallback. Also built the failure text from the SAME constants the resolver probes (installedPackageSearchPaths / describeInstalledPackageSearch), so a message can never name a path the code did not search. packageName and exists are injectable so the scoped behaviour runs now rather than for the first time on the release that depends on it. Four mutation proofs, each diffed against the pre-mutation file and re-read from disk before the red was believed. Left BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPT_VALUE in lib/init.mjs alone and named it in the guard's failure text — same defect, but it writes into the consumer's package.json, so it travels with the rename. Issue #625.
